case_name: Navtej Singh Johar and Others v. Union of India

pages.text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CONSTITUTION BENCH
Navtej Singh Johar and Others ... Petitioners
versus
Union of India ... Respondent
Coram: Dipak Misra, C.J., R.F. Nariman, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra, JJ.
Judgment Dated: 06 September 2018

DIPAK MISRA, C.J.:
1. The petitioners challenged the constitutional validity of Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 in so far as it criminalises consensual carnal intercourse against the order of nature between consenting adults in private.

2. Constitutional Morality over Majoritarian Morality: Sexual orientation is an innate aspect of individual privacy, dignity and personal autonomy protected under Articles 14, 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution. Constitutional morality must trump social morality.

3. Decision: Section 377 of the Indian Penal Code is unconstitutional to the extent it penalises consensual sexual relations between consenting adults in private. Non-consensual carnal intercourse and sexual offences against minors or animals continue to remain governed by Section 377 IPC and relevant penal statutes.
